title: Acasta Gneiss, oldest known rocks (c. 4.03 Ga)
summary: Exposed along the Acasta River in Canada's Northwest Territories, tonalitic and granodioritic orthogneisses of the Acasta Gneiss Complex yielded zircon uranium-lead ages of 4.00 to 4.03 billion years, with the International Commission on Stratigraphy fixing the Hadean-Archean boundary at 4031 ± 3 million years. As Earth's oldest known coherent rock formation, the complex records the transition from primordial mafic crust to evolved continental crust.

uncertainty.note: Chronostratigraphic boundary uncertainty on the base of the Archean (4031 ± 3 Ma) from U-Pb dating of the Idiwhaa tonalitic orthogneiss in the Acasta Gneiss Complex (ICS Chronostratigraphic Chart v2024/12; Bowring and Williams 1999).

as_recorded.value: Priscoan (4.00–4.03 Ga) orthogneisses from northwestern Canada

where.modern_name: Acasta River area, Slave Craton, Northwest Territories, Canada

importance.justification: The Acasta Gneiss Complex preserves Earth's oldest known intact rock units, providing physical evidence for early crustal differentiation and defining the formal chronological boundary between the Hadean and Archean eons.

related.because: Planetary cooling and early crustal differentiation formed the magmatic protoliths of the Acasta gneisses.
